answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a small, nontransferable stake by completing a sequence of tasks witnessed by randomly selected, established peers. A peer’s attestation is weighted by its own history, so a cluster of fresh accounts cannot vouch for itself; colluding endorsements form a detectable ripple across the trust graph, while honest reputations create a ridge of costly-to-forge evidence. The attacker must spend time and resources building each identity’s thread of credible interactions, rather than minting unlimited accounts at negligible cost.
